faq.a: Coloured molecules contain a group of atoms that absorbs certain colours of light. The colours that are not absorbed bounce back to your eyes, and that is the colour you see.

faq.q: What is the chemical in household bleach?
faq.a: Most household bleach is sodium hypochlorite dissolved in water. Oxygen bleaches use hydrogen peroxide instead, which is gentler on colours.

faq.q: Why should bleach never be mixed with other cleaners?
faq.a: Mixed with acidic cleaners it gives off chlorine gas, and with ammonia it gives off chloramine gases. Both are poisonous to breathe.
asks: Is it dangerous to mix bleach?

faq.q: Does bleach remove the stain or just hide it?
faq.a: Mostly it changes the stain's molecules so they no longer absorb light. The changed molecules may still be there but are colourless, so the stain seems to vanish.
As a strong oxidiser, bleach damages the proteins and other molecules that germs need to survive, so it kills bacteria and many viruses.

facts: Household chlorine bleach is a dilute solution of sodium hypochlorite in water.
Mixing bleach with ammonia or acidic cleaners releases toxic gases.
